defects: Input and fallback domains, exact rejection/value identity and zero-timeout ordering were unstated.

Author constant wrapper/timer work rather than treating elapsed waiting as computation. Add original object/function/Symbol/NaN/-0 values, frozen rejection identity, all fallback shapes, immediate fresh native result and late-settlement stability.

objective: Buffer asynchronous outcomes by original index and flush each newly ready prefix without waiting for later slots.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Ordered rendering can progress before a slower final section.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Capturing run membership and amortized prefix flushing transfer to streaming work.

relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A mutable length or an uncaught rendering callback can leave completion pending forever.

defects: Reference read caller-mutable promises.length after invocation.
Reference/junior did not reject the completion promise when show threw.
Senior bypassed the expressly taught forEach/slot/while approach.
Exact outcome identity, callback arity, frozen membership and total amortized work were unstated.
rationale: Make all boards use immediate native-promise subscriptions, captured total, per-index outcome objects and a while-based prefix flush. Callback-throw behavior is a newly explicit policy; mutable-length acceptance was an existing functional gap. Simultaneous empty and nonempty runs plus a nested callback-started run verify independent state.

objective: Await two numeric promises in the authored first-then-second order and forward the original rejection reason.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Async functions and await remain standard JavaScript syntax.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Combining eventual numeric values is a small practical async task.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ordered consumption versus fail-fast aggregation is a transferable distinction.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Two explicit awaits isolate the lesson from array aggregation.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Using Promise.all changes which rejection wins and whether a pending first input holds the result.

defects: Senior used Promise.all while the prompt, skeleton and other boards taught first then second awaits.
Both-reject ordering and an early second rejection while first remains pending were unspecified.
Numeric bounds, signed zero, exact arbitrary rejection identity and producer-start semantics were unstated.
rationale: Align senior to sequential awaits. Make the already intended method explicit: first rejection has priority, second is observed after first fulfills, and producer creation need not be serialized. Bound finite Number fulfillments to absolute 1e16, preserve signed-zero addition and arbitrary original rejection reasons, return a fresh native promise and explain the caller/checks pre-handle a potentially early second rejection. State O(1) wrapper work/state excluding waiting/producers. Add delayed-first versus earlier-second failures, a never-settling first input, exact frozen second failure, fractions/cancellation/signed zero and immediate promise identity. Treat rejection-priority cases as a clarified authored exercise policy, not a claim that concurrent aggregation is generally wrong.
